body: The FedRAMP OSCAL mandate effective 30 September 2026 requires federal cloud authorization to be expressed in machine-readable, continuously verifiable artifacts — not PDF attestations. The Council of AI produces verified measurement credentials for AI-system containment; it does not claim to 'certify' a vendor as FedRAMP-authorized (that authority sits with the US General Services Administration). The correct procurement framing: the Council of AI supplies an independently measured containment profile that a FedRAMP-authorized assessor can reference during an OSCAL-structured assessment. The board provides 14 axes (detection, care, denial, governance, synthetic-content provenance) measured against 19+ frontier models; each manifest signed Ed25519 and frozen at a timestamp. Each observation binds to the manifest, making it independently verifiable without vendor assertion. The language binds: monitored containment (continuous signed measurement, not a one-time isolation proof); verified measurement credential (measurement tied to a fixed manifest, not a marketing claim). Buyer-facing surfaces show DEFONEOS umbrella / meok-defoneos (build) / csoai-defoneos (certify) / DEFONEOS-SEAL (credential). The defense-AI compartment doctrine keeps meok-defoneos, csoai-defoneos, and dagon strictly separated — never cross-linked; dagon is NDA-only and never linked to meok.ai or csoai.org. No kinetic-targeting, personal-surveillance, 'AUKUS partnership', or 'DAIC certified' claims; no defonos.io reference; DEFONEOS-SEAL requires 33-agent BFT council vote (quorum 23/33).
